machine: Apple M3 Mac15,13 macOS26.2; eight physical CPUs; compilers, tests and profilers idle during latency and resource cohorts
protocol: Fresh processes; reverse order on alternate rounds; every invocation computes all posts; full parsed JSON equality against unchanged standard Rust. All initial runs retained; no outlier removal.
limitations: Processing timers exclude JSON IO. Mech input admission is recorded separately; upstream input decoding is outside their timers.
Mech accounting and checked arithmetic remain enabled. Cleanup and worker-pool lifetime follow each adapter; consult the per-variant timing boundary.
Single-core standard, specialized algorithms and concurrent implementations are labeled separately.
Parent wall_seconds covers fresh subprocess launch through exit, including restoration, JSON IO, admission and cleanup; it includes common subprocess-launch overhead.

timing_boundaries.upstream: Original upstream timer, with global pool preinitialized, retained only as a labeled historical reference.
timing_boundaries.matched_worker_lifecycle: Both implementations create, run and join workers inside processing; JSON decoding excluded. Mech admission is additional and separately reported.
timing_boundaries.whole_process: Parent monotonic clock around fresh subprocess launch through exit, including JSON IO, artifact restoration, admission, computation and teardown. OS file cache is not flushed.
timing_boundaries.post_json: One continuous interval includes input preparation and allocations plus computation and worker create/run/join. Mech supplies post_json_seconds; Rust supplies its documented processing timer. JSON IO and Mech artifact restoration are included in the separate complete-process measurement.

whole_process_reference.scope: Fastest external fresh process, launch through exit, including all setup, JSON IO, computation and teardown.

matched_native_reference.scope: Fastest explicitly documented post-JSON timer including input preparation and worker creation/run/join. Artifact restoration and JSON IO are tracked in whole-process time.

fastest_reference.scope: Historical raw processing timer convention; preparation and worker lifetimes may differ. This is not the primary comparison.

primary_reference.scope: Fastest external fresh process, launch through exit, including all setup, JSON IO, computation and teardown.

primary_metric_definition: Lower is faster. The headline ratio always measures a complete fresh process, launch through exit, including all preparation, restoration, allocation, JSON IO and teardown. Secondary post-JSON ratios require explicit compatible boundary declarations and one continuous interval including Mech admission and intervening setup. Unknown or preinitialized processing timers never qualify as matched references. Neither an excluded startup cost nor a favorable partial interval establishes complete-task parity.
